assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guidance Rs180-190 cr (CFO, May-2026; new products, replacement, upgrades); cash capex Rs146 cr in FY26 and Rs128-198 cr in FY23-FY26. FY28-29E rise for ESC assembly and Oragadam expansion ('further expansions, we will be doing in Oragadam').

cover.headline: The incumbent for India's 2027 truck-safety rules, priced for most of it
cover.lead: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India (the former WABCO India, 60% owned by ZF) makes the air brakes in most Indian trucks and buses, sells spares, and exports goods and engineering services to its parent. Revenue grew 7.5% in FY26 and 9.3% in Q1FY27, but the Q1 margin fell to 12.9% on aluminium costs and FY26's ₹61 cr of FX gains will not repeat. We forecast EPS (post-bonus) of ₹44.2 / ₹54.1 / ₹63.4 for FY27-29E, with the step-up when ESC becomes mandatory on all trucks from Oct-2027. The street values ZF CV on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (Anand Rathi 50x Mar-28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since 2021, 47.7x, cut by the 7.8% auto-component de-rating) gives **44x Sep-28E EPS of ₹58.8 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,341, DCF ₹1,306. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A real moat, and regulation is about to widen it
arguments.p: ZF CV India has supplied Indian truck makers' air brakes for six decades and the ZF group claims ~80% of CV braking in India. ESC has been mandatory on most buses since Sep-2025; from Oct-2027 every truck and bus above 6 tonnes needs ESC and five ADAS functions. ZF holds pneumatic ESC nominations from three major OEMs and full ADAS-suite awards from two. We model OEM revenue +18% in FY28E and +15% in FY29E.

arguments.h: But the next twelve months are about costs and the cycle
arguments.p: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin was 12.9%: aluminium went from ~₹260 to >₹360/kg and OEMs pay back with a lag ("over the next quarter"). The CFO's May outlook was "flattish... single-digit small growth". Trucks above 6 tonnes grew 16.6% in FY26, so the base is high, and a rule that raises truck prices in 2027 may pull demand forward. FY27E EPS is flat on FY26 in our model.

arguments.h: A third of revenue is with the parent, on the parent's terms
arguments.p: Goods exports (₹1,025 cr, −11% in FY26 on US tariffs) and engineering services (₹504 cr, +11%) go mostly to ZF CV Systems Global at cost-plus prices: ₹1,351 cr of transactions in FY26, with ₹2,500 cr approved for FY27. Royalty is 2.5% of revenue. This cushions the Indian cycle but caps the margin, and ZF has sold 15% of the company since 2024.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair, with the street's Buys assuming 50x
arguments.p: At ₹2,341 the stock trades at 43.2x our FY28E and 39.8x Sep-28E EPS, below its own 47.7x forward median since 2021, with ₹2,177 cr of net cash inside. Auto-component stocks sat 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. The four standing broker targets (median ₹2,967) are all Buy; Anand Rathi's 50x on its higher pre-squeeze EPS (FY28E ₹62.6 vs our ₹54.1) explains the gap.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): margin recovery after the July price increases and OEM cost settlements; Jul-Sep truck volumes.
ESC/ADAS: more OEM nominations, homologation at the ZF Proving Ground, and the start of localised ESC production ahead of Oct-2027.
Exports: US truck production and tariffs; new North American actuator and disc-brake-chamber programmes; the India-EU trade agreement.
The parent: further stake sales by WABCO Asia (60.00%), new engineering or sourcing work moved to India, and any change to the payout policy.
Metal prices: aluminium had eased ~₹25/kg in July from its >₹360/kg peak.

sections.title: The air brakes in most Indian trucks and buses, plus exports and engineering for its German parent

blocks.p: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India (the former WABCO India) makes the systems that brake and manage compressed air in trucks, buses, trailers, tractors and construction machines: compressors, valves, brake actuators and chambers, ABS, and now electronic braking (EBS), electronic stability control (ESC), air suspension (ECAS), clutch actuation for automated gearboxes and bus door controls. It has supplied Indian truck makers for six decades and is the incumbent on almost every heavy truck and bus platform. Its promoter, WABCO Asia (Singapore), owns 60% and belongs to ZF Friedrichshafen, which bought WABCO worldwide in 2020.

Revenue comes from four places. **Domestic OEM** sales to truck, bus and tractor makers (₹1,978 cr in FY26, 48.0%). **Aftermarket** spares through ~550 dealers and distributors (₹584 cr, 14.2%). **Exports of goods** (₹1,025 cr, 24.9%), mostly compressors and actuators made in the Chennai SEZ; ₹781 cr of them were sold to one sister company, ZF CV Systems Global GmbH, which distributes them to ZF's plants and customers in the US and Europe. **Services** (₹504 cr, 12.2%): software, R&D and support work done in India for ZF's global commercial-vehicle division, billed at cost plus a mark-up. In all, ~₹1,351 cr of business (a third of revenue) was with that one group company.

sections.title: From TVS brakes division to a ZF subsidiary; the parent has been selling down since 2024

blocks.p: The company began as the brakes division of Sundaram-Clayton in 1962, using WABCO technology, and became a separately listed WABCO subsidiary. ZF bought WABCO worldwide in 2020 and renamed the Indian company in 2022. Two things since then matter for valuation. First, the parent has reduced its stake from 75% to 60% in three steps (Jun-2024, Dec-2024, Jun-2025), adding supply to a once-illiquid stock. Second, the 5:1 bonus of Jun-2026 multiplied the share count by six: every per-share number in this report is on the new basis (FY26 EPS ₹45.4, not ₹272.7).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** in India this is one of the few auto-component franchises with a genuine moat: safety-critical systems, validated on each platform, with a dominant installed base, an aftermarket tail and a regulatory pipeline (ESC, ADAS) it is best placed to win. sections.title: Revenue doubled from the Covid trough; margins back to ~16%, a fifth of pre-tax profit is treasury and FX income

blocks.p: ZF CV India's revenue was ₹2,854 cr in FY19, fell to ₹1,864 cr in FY21 (BS-VI and Covid emptied truck factories) and reached ₹4,119 cr in FY26: 17% a year from the trough, 5% a year from the FY19 peak. The truck cycle explains most of it. FY25 was a flat year (revenue +0.4%); in FY26 truck and bus production above 6 tonnes grew 16.6% after the GST cut. The mix also changed: services billed to ZF (₹504 cr) and goods exported to ZF (₹781 cr to one group company) are now ~30% of revenue. The EBITDA margin (excluding other income) recovered from 10% in FY22 to 15-16.5% in FY24-26, close to the 14-16% of FY15-FY19 but no higher. EPS (post-bonus) went from ₹24.8 (FY19) to ₹45.4 (FY26); other income, mostly interest on a ₹2,200 cr cash pile plus FX gains, was 25% of FY26 pre-tax profit.

bullets: **Cash conversion is lumpy, not weak.** Cash from operations was 48% of net profit in FY24, 62% in FY25 and 157% in FY26 (₹810 cr): receivables from ZF CV Systems Global rose to ₹437 cr at Mar-25 and fell to ₹192 cr at Mar-26. **FX gains inflate some years.** FY26 other income of ₹183 cr included ₹61 cr of FX gains (₹39 cr in Q1FY26 alone, on services billed in euros at an old rate) and a ₹10 cr reversal of credit-loss provisions. blocks.p: Coverage is thin and uniformly positive. After Q1FY27 ICICI Securities kept Buy with ₹2,800 (28-Jul-2026), calling the quarter operationally "muted" (margin 190bp below its estimate) but expecting higher content to drive growth. ICICI Direct's last note before our date (24-Jun-2026, after the bonus) has Buy and ₹3,170. Anand Rathi's latest visible note (13-Feb-2026) has Buy and ₹18,800 before the bonus (₹3,133 after), at **50x Mar-28E P/E**; Geojit's last note (Sep-2025) was Accumulate at ₹2,624 post-bonus. Median of the four standing targets: ₹2,967, +27% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹2,341. The one broker whose method we can see (Anand Rathi) uses **P/E on one-year-forward EPS**; the others' methods are behind logins, but their targets sit at 45-54x our Sep-28E EPS, consistent with P/E. The bulls focus on the ESC/ADAS mandate and the truck cycle; nobody in our sources is negative.
